title: VANKO-ABDUCTED-ZEBRAFISH: Anatomy of an Insider Data Theft
subtitle: Reconstructing the kill chain — from a disguised account to secure-wiped tracks, recovered from the snapshots he forgot
intro_line: Ten artifacts trace one employee's path from quiet setup to the deliberate cover-up of classified-data theft.
outro_line: He wiped the staging archive ten times over — but old shadow-copy snapshots preserved the proof he tried to erase.

cards.headline: Tor and network-scanning tools installed, then deleted
cards.proves: The subject installed anonymity and network-scanning tools on the work desktop and deleted them, showing intent to hide his activity.

cards.headline: Hidden 'defaultprinter' account created for theft
cards.proves: A disguised user account was created to quietly stage the stolen files under a name meant to look like a harmless printer.

cards.headline: Vanko's PC reached the secret-files server directly
cards.proves: His computer connected straight to the StarkResearch file server that held the stolen company secrets.

cards.headline: He opened Level-12 secret "Project Nehemiah"
cards.proves: The subject opened a top-tier classified document, exceeding the access he was supposed to have.

cards.headline: Stolen secrets staged in 'temp.zip' on disguised account
cards.proves: A fake "defaultprinter" account held a 2.6MB archive of classified weapon and DNA research on its desktop, proving the subject used a disguised account to collect and stage stolen company secrets.

cards.headline: Vanko replied to foreign recruiter, attached 3 files
cards.proves: Vanko was in two-way contact with a foreign recruiter and sent that channel a reply carrying three attachments.

cards.headline: Files packed with 7-Zip, then secure-wiped 10 times
cards.proves: Vanko ran 7-Zip to bundle the data and then ran SDelete ten times to securely erase traces, the hallmark of deliberate theft and cover-up rather than routine maintenance.

cards.headline: Disguised archive uploaded to Dropbox
cards.proves: Usage records confirm the disguised archive was sent out through Dropbox and OneDrive, the channels used to remove the stolen data.

cards.headline: Deleted 1.9GB Dropbox folder 2 minutes after upload
cards.proves: Right after sending the stolen files out, he deleted the local copy to hide what he had taken.

cards.headline: Wipe-tool tracks recovered from Shadow Copies
cards.proves: The subject ran a secure-wipe tool to destroy the stolen-data staging archive and erase the proof it had run, but old backup snapshots preserved the deleted evidence.
